preview: Mridul Sharma shares his interview experience for the summer analyst intern position at Citi, detailing the coding test, technical round with OOP and puzzles, and the HR round.
content: INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE Hey Buddy, if you are reading this interview experience then I believe you are doing quite well in your interview prep. I am Mridul Sharma - BTech IT - 2024 Batch - currently residing in the hostel. In my 3rd year before getting into Citi as a summer analyst intern I got a chance in BNY Mellon too. So let me share my experience during my BNY interview. Anyways just to let you know, I have stammered a lot since my childhood and if you too have any kind of special ability like me then you can relate with me. BNY Mellon - Coding test: 1 hard 3D DP question + 1 medium array question + 1 priority queue question. ( I hardly remember what were they ). I did 2 and a half question and got into the technical interview round. So I suggest to get good in DP (1D and 2D atleast), arrays and strings, binary search, heaps and Trees. Doing atleast 50 questions of each topic from Leetcode will work. Tech Round1 - Started with a good intro with some stammer but the interviewer told me to relax and not to worry about the stammer as he will not judge me on that ( honestly that was well needed feedback for me, you may not relate though). He went through my resume and started off with my skill section. Interviewer : Oh! You do C++. Great. Let’s start with OOP. Are you confident in it. I affirmed and then he asked me 5-6 questions on c++ OOP. Questions on : virtual functions, pure virtual functions, objects, inheritance were asked. Then two coding questions: 1. Given a binary 2D matrix with just two rows same. Identify those two rows. Expected time complexity is O(n^2). I thought for a while and gave him both brute force and optimal approaches. 2. String based question. Check if strings are isomorphic or not. I didn’t know what isomorphic string are, so I asked and gave him the optimal solution. Then a very little discussion on project and that’s it. I was shortlisted for Round2. Tech Round2 + HR - Started with project discussions and he asked me about my contributions in the project specifically. Then SQL advanced questions like stored procedures ( that I was not able to answer at that time), triggers etc. Medium difficulty OOP question with a lot of inherited classes, some virtual functions and pure virtual functions in the base class. He asked me to make an object of a derived class and correct any error in the output. Unfortunately I failed to do so in time and didn’t make it to selection. Advice - Prepare the basic things like OOP in depth with implementation that too with your own hands. Stay calm and maintain a friendly two way conversation with the interviewer. Keep a little confident smile in the whole interview. Flex some of your extracurricular skills in your intro and that’s all. Citi - Coding Test - 1 easy pattern printing question + 1 medium graph question (practice graph question and algos like BFS, DFS and djiktras). I solved the 1st one and the 2nd question was only able pass some 7/11 test cases. Tech Round 1 - Started off with my intro and it went well. She asked me some 2-3 OOP questions. Same virtual functions and stuff. Then out of nowhere she asked me 2 puzzles ( I was a little shocked) Puzzle 1 - 2 Balls Puzzle 2 - water jug problem I knew the trick behind the first puzzle but was unfamiliar with the 2nd one. Did a little brainstorming and gave her the answer. She was impressed and I got into the HR round, HR round - Started with a brief intro and she asked me about my friends and family. A little discussion on projects, then I asked about her experience at citi and that’s it. I cleared the HR round and got selected for Citi. Advice - Somehow show the interviewer that you are an excellent team leader and you can work in teams to complete the work before time ( You can show this while explaining your projects or telling him about your role in committee or any club ). Answer everything honestly, try to make a good eye contact with the interviewer, and show your curiosity and interest towards knowing and joining the company,
